answer: Each agent must lock spendable stake into a shared settlement lagoon and keep a public lantern lit: a signed, epoch-fresh receipt of unique peer-attested work. The lantern's fuel is a one-time ember, a work digest no other address has published. Peers refuse to attest a lantern whose ember collides with another claim, and both depositors are slashed from the lagoon. Creating sybils therefore requires a full lagoon deposit and a unique work ember for every fake identity, so attack cost tracks scarce capital and real work, not cheap key generation.
